visual_elements.description: Generic 2x2 confusion matrix. Header 'Predicted as' spans columns P and N; left side is labeled 'Actual'. Row P contains TP under P and FN under N. Row N contains FP under P and TN under N. TP and TN are green-filled; FN and FP are yellow-filled.
Numeric confusion matrix at Threshold=0.5. Same structure: Actual rows P and N; Predicted as columns P and N. Cells are P/P=4, P/N=1, N/P=1, N/N=5. Red grid/border styling with black numerals.
Small red-outlined box/label with red text 'Threshold=0.5'.

visual_elements.description: Beige rounded-rectangle pipeline. Left: 'Test Sample' label above a small airplane icon, arrow pointing right into a red filled 'Model' box. Under Model: red text '[Any value] – (0, +1)'. Arrow points right to a blue-bordered white box '(0 — 1)'. Above this area is red text 'Predicted Value'. Arrow points right to a red-bordered white box 'Threshold (e.g. 0.5)'. From the threshold box, two arrows branch to a green oval 'Class I' and a pink oval 'Class II'.

Predicted-value number line. Red horizontal axis labeled 0.0 at left, 0.5 at center, and 1.0 at right. A blue dashed vertical line rises at 0.5 with a red dot on the axis. Multiple line-drawn airplane icons are scattered left and right of the line; plain airplanes are mostly left of 0.5 and skull-marked airplanes mostly right, with the placement matching the 4/1/1/5 confusion-matrix counts.

recreation_brief: 1) Use a white 16:9 slide. Add the exact title 'Effect of Selecting Threshold Value on Model Performance' at the top in large bold dark red (#C00000). Place a yellow circle (#FFFF00) at the top-right with black text '24'. 2) In the upper-left, build the generic confusion matrix: columns P and N under a merged 'Predicted as' header, rows P and N under an 'Actual' side label; fill TP/TN green (#00B050) with white text and FN/FP yellow (#FFFF00) with black text. 3) Below it, build the numeric matrix with the same P/N structure and cells 4, 1, 1, 5 using red borders. 4) Add a red-outlined label 'Threshold=0.5' to the right of the matrices. 5) Draw a beige (#FFF2CC) rounded rectangle pipeline: 'Test Sample' with a small airplane icon, arrow to a red (#C00000) 'Model' box, red sub-label '[Any value] – (0, +1)', arrow to a blue-bordered (#0070C0) box '(0 — 1)', red label 'Predicted Value' above, arrow to a red-bordered box 'Threshold (e.g. 0.5)', then two arrows to a green (#00B050) oval 'Class I' and a pink (#FF99CC) oval 'Class II'. 6) At the bottom, draw a red horizontal axis from 0.0 to 1.0 with tick labels 0.0, 0.5, 1.0; add a blue dashed vertical line at 0.5 and a red dot where it meets the axis. 7) Scatter airplane icons around the axis: left of 0.5 place five icons representing predicted P/Class I, right of 0.5 place six icons representing predicted N/Class II; use plain airplanes for actual P and skull-marked airplanes for actual N so the counts match TP=4, FN=1, FP=1, TN=5. 8) Ignore the black bar at the very bottom; it is video-player UI, not slide content.
